sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `readLength` returns -1 for `0x80` indefinite length which flows into `new byte[length]` as `NegativeArraySizeException`. WHY: Declared `throws IOException` callers (`readInteger`, `readNext`) leak an unchecked crash on attacker-controlled DER instead of a checked failure. HOW: Reject `0x80` with `IOException` since DER requires definite lengths.

WHAT: `readSequence` subtracts full TLV sizes from content length without checking for negative overshoot or trailing bytes. WHY: Malformed ECDSA DER with extra/truncated elements passes the `size==2` check and is normalized to a different valid signature, enabling signature malleability. HOW: Fail when `length` goes negative, is nonzero at exit, or bytes remain after the sequence.

WHAT: `integerToBytes` zero-pads negative `BigInteger` values and truncates oversized ones instead of rejecting them. WHY: Attacker-crafted DER with negative r/s is converted to a different positive fixed-length value that then verifies, breaking strict DER validation. HOW: Reject `signum()<0` and `bitLength` overflow with `IOException`.

WHAT: `create()` initializes the process-wide once-only `CryptoIntegration` with the authz-client classloader whose service file sees only the weak `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`. WHY: If called first in a shared JVM, later server init becomes a no-op and all server crypto calls hit `UnsupportedOperationException` stubs. HOW: Init with the thread-context classloader that sees all providers instead of the narrow classloader.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.
Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.
Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes the -1 returned by readLength for indefinite-length encoding to read(int), which allocates new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException on malformed DER input.
integerToBytes silently truncates r/s values longer than the curve size, so non-canonical DER signatures are accepted as different values (signature malleability).
AuthzClient.create eagerly initializes CryptoIntegration, so a shaded/repackaged client that lost its ServiceLoader file fails at construction instead of only when ECDSA is used.

Calling CryptoIntegration.init from AuthzClient.create is claimed to lock the global crypto provider to the minimal AuthzClientCryptoProvider so a later server init is ignored and unsupported operations fail.
The ignored-providers message is passed to logger.debugf as a format string instead of using logger.debug, and keeps a trailing comma.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Organization link/unlink does not invalidate the getForLogin cache even though login eligibility depends on organizationId. WHY: Leaves stale REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL login lists showing realm brokers that became org-private or hiding newly linked brokers after OrganizationProvider membership changes.

WHAT: New login predicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without null-check. WHY: Throws NPE during create/remove/update invalidation when a transient IdentityProviderModel has null config, breaking IDP writes.

WHAT: Single revisioned login entry accumulates one map entry per distinct organizationId and copies the whole map on each new org. WHY: Causes unbounded cluster object growth and O(orgs) copy cost on every first query per org.

issues.descricao: Claims getForLogin re-enters the caching layer by calling session.identityProviders().getById instead of idpDelegate.getById; this deliberately resolves IDs through the per-IDP cache.
Claims the cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw, non-organization-aware models; getById already wraps them.
Claims linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization never invalidates the getForLogin caches; the org provider routes through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update which does.
Claims resolving cached IDs one by one with getById turns login listing into N lookups; those lookups hit the per-IDP cache by design.
Claims the HashSet in cached getForLogin returns IDPs in nondeterministic order; every caller sorts the result.
Claims remove() of a nonexistent alias now dereferences null; the new login invalidation is null-safe and the other call is unchanged pre-existing code.
Claims getLoginPredicate can NPE on a null config; config is always initialized.
Claims org-specific ALL/ORG_ONLY login queries include non-public org IDPs, so the BROKER_PUBLIC gate misses invalidations; the query always requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true.

getForLogin caches all organizations under one realm/mode entry, so each new organizationId invalidates and rebuilds that entry with every previously cached search merged in, instead of caching per organization.

Disabling an organization does not invalidate the cached login IDP lists in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin, so callers that do not re-check isEnabled could get IDPs of a disabled organization.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The removal listener invokes V2 setPermissionsEnabled which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: Any client/role/group deletion while V2 is active aborts with an exception from the event listener.
WHAT: getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every Clients resource. WHY: Listing/filtering cost grows linearly with client count and each evaluation is expensive.

issues.descricao: Claims the per-client resource lookup uses server.getId() as owner while resources are created with server.getClientId(), so client-specific permissions are never found.
Claims that with both fine-grained features enabled, client deletion calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims the all-clients resource lookup in hasPermission(String) cannot find the resource (owner mismatch or not lazily created), so global client permissions are ignored.
Claims the client management-permissions endpoint returns a 500 under V2 because it calls ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException.
Claims hasPermission(client, scope) accepts permissions granted on other resources because it does not filter by resource id, allowing privilege escalation across clients.
Claims getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every client resource, causing O(N) slowdowns.
ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation for every client resource of type Clients, so listing clients costs one evaluation per client resource.

On ClientRemovedEvent the AdminPermissions listener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2 when V1 and V2 are both enabled, so client deletion fails.
Claims that with both fine-grained authz V1 and V2 enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which now throws, so client deletion fails.
Claims the test grants CONFIGURE together with MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, so addComposites may succeed because of CONFIGURE and the test would pass even if canMapCompositeRoles were broken.
Claims that under FGAP V2 the client management-permissions GET/PUT endpoints call the throwing ClientPermissionsV2 overrides and return 500.

ClientPermissionsV2 canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles check only fine-grained permissions and not the manage-clients role, claimed to deny role mapping to realm admins unlike V1.
Claims the canView(ClientModel) Javadoc is misleading because V2 never evaluates the per-client VIEW_SCOPE permission.
Claims the tests index getDefaultClientScopes() without size checks and could throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `emailValidation` depends on `rejectedEmails.@each` but the array holds plain strings. WHY: `pushObject` of a string does not trigger `@each`, so the email field does not re-validate after a server rejection.

WHAT: `should_block?` is never called when a whitelist/blacklist error is already present, so its `match_count`/`last_match_at` update is skipped. WHY: Match statistics undercount and `last_match_at` goes stale for blocked addresses that also violate domain lists. HOW: Separate the stats increment from the error-adding guard so the lookup always runs.

issues.descricao: Claims the rejected-email memory stores the server-normalised email, so it never matches the raw input on retry.
Claims the 'rejectedEmails.@each' dependent key does not observe pushes of plain strings, so the rejection is not shown until the email changes.
BlockedEmail.should_block? returns nil instead of false when the email has no record.
Claims EmailValidator dropped the email format check that the old User#email_validator performed, allowing invalid emails.
Claims EmailValidator#email_in_restriction_setting? raises NoMethodError when the email is nil.
Claims the blocked-email validator specs would still pass if the blocked-email branch were removed.

`rejectedEmails` is declared as an array literal on the controller prototype, so it is shared across instances and modal sessions; emails rejected once keep failing validation later. Initialize it per instance in `init`.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was renumbered from 4 to 3 while FEATURE_DISABLED reuses 4. WHY: The guide tells automation to rely only on the check exit code, so existing scripts polling for 4 as recreate now misclassify recreate as feature-disabled. HOW: Keep RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE at 4 and assign a fresh code to FEATURE_DISABLED.

WHAT: Feature-disabled path calls picocli.exit(4) then returns without setting a Quarkus exit code. WHY: Picocli.exit() is a no-op in test launch mode (Picocli.java:203-208), so embedded and test runs report exit 0 success despite the error. HOW: Throw a mapped exception or set the exit code via the command spec instead of relying on System.exit side effect.

WHAT: createInitialDeployment returns early for null strategy without enabling rolling-updates. WHY: The null-strategy parametrized runs then test a different CR shape than documented required config, hiding operator failure or upgrade-decision divergence. HOW: Enable the ROLLING_UPDATES feature before the null early-return or document why null is exempt.

issues.descricao: Claims the rolling-updates feature is not enabled for the null update strategy in UpgradeTest, so that case tests the operator without the gated feature.
Claims RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 and 4 now means feature disabled, a breaking change that needs release notes.
Claims calling picocli.exit() for the disabled-feature exit code is incorrect because it calls System.exit directly.
Claims `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` in UpdateCompatibilityCheck can hit a null profile and throw NullPointerException because initProfile is skipped for update-compatibility.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Shard entry switched from `interpolateVariablesInQueries` (full replace) to `applyTemplateVariables` (strips `__auto/__range/__interval` for backend). WHY: Split-time sharding checks and shard-selector extraction now operate on uninterpolated variables, changing which queries shard and what selector is sent to `fetchLabelValues`.

issues.descricao: Claims interpolating before partitioning substitutes $__range so range queries are wrongly split; applyTemplateVariables leaves $__range untouched.
Notes test coverage of the new interpolation; no issue.
Notes test coverage of shard interpolation; no issue.
The interpolation test hardcodes the number of applyTemplateVariables calls, making it brittle to unrelated splitting changes.
The new interpolation tests do not set request.filters, so passing ad hoc filters to applyTemplateVariables is untested.
runShardSplitQuery now uses applyTemplateVariables, which strips __auto/__range scoped vars, so queries with [$__auto] reach shard sub-requests uninterpolated and fail.
Switching shard splitting from interpolateVariablesInQueries to applyTemplateVariables drops the datasource ref on each split query, claimed to leave stale or missing datasource for routing.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `ProvideAnonDBStore` now requires a bare `int64` deviceLimit that Wire cannot inject, while `pkg/server/wire.go:374` still lists it as a provider. WHY: Breaks Wire generation/resolution and leaves a second orphan `AnonStore` instance divergent from the manually built one in `impl.go:43`. HOW: Remove the stale `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` entry from the Wire set.

issues.descricao: Claims ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 parameter breaks wire dependency injection because wire.go still registers it.
Claims updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-row update, conflating missing or stale devices with the limit being reached.
Claims anonymous clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the X-Grafana-Device-Id header.
Claims anonymous authentication now fails entirely when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, instead of the previous non-blocking async tagging.
Claims TagDevice now propagates all tagging errors instead of only the limit error, breaking callers that ignored them.
Claims updateDevice's time window is based on device.UpdatedAt rather than time.Now(), which may not match the intended logic.
ProvideAnonDBStore gained an int64 deviceLimit parameter but is still registered as a wire provider in pkg/server/wire.go, which has no provider for int64, so wire generation or compilation fails.

ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit but is still registered as a Wire provider (with an AnonStore bind) in pkg/server/wire.go; Wire cannot supply an int64, so DI generation and the server build fail.
Claims updateDevice's RowsAffected()==0 check wrongly denies already-registered devices on MySQL because MySQL reports changed rather than matched rows.
CreateOrUpdateDevice runs a full COUNT over the 30-day anon_device table on every anonymous request when a device limit is set.
The 'device limit reached' error string is hard-coded English and bypasses i18n.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `List` returns directly from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` on cache hit without the outdated-cache requery that `Check` added. WHY: Newly created dashboards/folders stay invisible in list results until `permCache` TTL expires, defeating the PR goal.

WHAT: `Check` short-circuits on `permDenialCache` hit and only sets denial on DB deny, never deleting it on later allow. WHY: A grant within the TTL window stays denied for the full TTL because the fresh-permission path is never reached.

WHAT: Denial entries are keyed per `(user, action, name, parent)` while `permCache` is per `(user, action)`. WHY: Enumeration or high deny traffic creates O(users x resources) entries in the shared local cache, evicting useful entries and growing memory every 30s window.

issues.descricao: Claims a cached denial blocks access granted within the TTL window; denials are TTL-bounded like the existing permission cache.
Claims trusting cached grants while re-checking cached denials lets stale grants keep access to revoked resources; cached grants were already served for the TTL before this PR.
Claims per-resource denial entries cause unbounded cache memory growth; entries expire after the short TTL.
Claims List now serves stale cached permissions whereas it previously always queried the DB; List was already cache-backed before the change.

Claims the new denial cache is checked before any permission source and never invalidated, so a Check that ran before a resource was created or a grant was added keeps returning Allowed:false for the whole short cache TTL.
Claims the remote authz client still wraps results in a 30s LocalCache, so in remote deployments new dashboards, folders and grants stay invisible for up to 30s.
Claims permissionCacheUsage counts a cache hit that did not grant access as a cache miss.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `remindersToCancel` queries all `cancelled:true` rows without filtering `method: EMAIL`. WHY: Any cancelled SMS row would be submitted as SendGrid `batch_id`, failing the request and tripping the batch-abort above. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` to the where clause.

issues.descricao: The booking-page reschedule path cancels email reminders with immediateDelete=true, which leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB, while the dashboard reschedule path marks it cancelled for cleanup, so the two flows are inconsistent.
Claims the code comment overstates the cancel window because the query lacks a lower bound on scheduledDate.
Claims the cron's cancel loop uses an undefined `client` variable, causing a ReferenceError.
Claims the unscheduled-reminders query re-schedules reminders marked cancelled because it lacks a cancelled filter.
Claims a hard-coded "Verification code" placeholder bypasses i18n.
Claims a hard-coded "Verify" button label bypasses i18n.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid send but neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row, leaving orphaned scheduled rows inconsistent with the non-immediate path.
Claims reminders from disabled event types are still sent and can be re-scheduled because they are only marked cancelled.
Notes the isSenderIdNeeded branch removal without reporting a problem.
The new cancelled column is nullable without a default, so existing WorkflowReminder rows get null instead of false.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row, and the callers no longer delete it, so reminder rows are left orphaned in the database.
The reschedule path cancels SendGrid email reminders immediately (immediateDelete=true) instead of flagging them cancelled for the cron, which supposedly accumulates cancelled batches.
When an email reminder is cancelled immediately on reschedule, its WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled, so stale scheduled reminder rows are left in the database.
Claims the cron's cancelled-reminders query can pick rows with a null referenceId and send batch_id:null to SendGrid, aborting cancellation of the remaining reminders.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Async legacy Create/Update/DeleteCollection capture live `obj`/`objInfo`/`options` pointers also returned to the caller. WHY: Concurrent serialization/mutation of the returned object races with the background legacy write. HOW: Deep-copy the object/options before capturing in the goroutine.

issues.descricao: Claims the Equal/NotEqual assertions in the Mode 3 tests can never fail, though the Equal assertion does fail if Delete stops returning the storage result.
Claims the legacy-create goroutine races with the caller on a shared obj that can alias the returned object.
Empty comment.
Every mode-3 write spawns an unbounded goroutine for the legacy store, risking goroutine and memory growth under load.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: ensure_embeddable authorizes solely on spoofable Referer header then sets X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL. WHY: Any client can forge Referer with curl to render embeds off-host and frame the forum anywhere, defeating the embeddable_host restriction.

WHAT: parent.postMessage targetOrigin is interpolated full request.referer URL instead of origin. WHY: Full URL with path never equals parent origin so resize messages are dropped and height sync breaks.

issues.descricao: Claims embed.js throws a TypeError when the page lacks the #discourse-comments element because comments.appendChild is called on null.
Claims the embed controller spec fails because EmbedController#best only enqueues a Sidekiq job and never constructs TopicRetriever during the request.
The hourly PollFeed job always fetches and processes the full feed without a conditional GET; the feed_key helper meant for that is defined but never used.
States that the link fallback in PollFeed is correct; no problem is reported.
States the raw_html cook_method comparison in Post#cook is safe; no problem is reported.
States the cook_method assignment in PostCreator is correct; no problem is reported.
States the `if topic_id` check in EmbedController is safe; no problem is reported.
Describes the host checks in ensure_embeddable without reporting a problem.
States content_sha1 and absolutize_urls in TopicEmbed are correct; no problem is reported.
States the TopicRetriever throttle uses setnx and an explicit no_throttle check; no problem is reported.
Claims import_remote passes an unvalidated user-supplied URL to Kernel#open, allowing command execution with '|' or local file reads.
Claims PollFeed fetches SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation, letting whoever controls that setting make the server request arbitrary internal or external URLs.
Claims the embed best.html.erb template closes its if block with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby, so every render raises a SyntaxError.
The embed layout interpolates request.referer into an inline JavaScript string with only HTML escaping, so a referer containing a quote can break out of the string and run script.
Claims postMessage drops the resize message because targetOrigin is the full referer URL rather than just the origin, breaking iframe auto-resize.
Claims setting X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL on the embed endpoint disables clickjacking protection and that the referer check can be spoofed.
Claims the cook_method migration default of 1 equals raw_html, so every post would skip cooking and sanitization.
Claims the 'not a url' TopicRetriever spec passes regardless of the InvalidURIError rescue because embeddable_host is blank.
`<%- end if %>` in embed/best.html.erb is not valid Ruby, so the template raises a SyntaxError and the embed page fails to render.
Claims `<%- end if %>` leaves a dangling if modifier that makes the logo output the condition, so the logo renders before the header button.
Claims the embed best action builds the view for current_user and then marks it publicly cacheable, so a staff member's view could be served to anonymous visitors.
fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without a presence check, raising NoMethodError when the setting is blank.
poll_feed opens the feed URL without a timeout and imports every item without a cap, so a slow or huge feed can tie up a worker.
The TopicRetriever specs mock perform_retrieve, so a bug in invalid_host? would not make them fail.
The EmbedController success tests only assert that mocks are called and would pass even if the controller logic were removed.
poll_feed has no test of feed parsing or TopicEmbed.import; the specs only check the execute guards.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `assignment_source.to_dict()` embeds a raw `datetime` into `apply_async` kwargs. WHY: The task payload must be JSON-serializable and `from_dict` rehydrates without type checks, so enqueue fails or `queued` round-trips as a str. HOW: Serialize `queued` to ISO string in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

WHAT: The new `assignment_source` base parameter has no matching parameter on `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound`. WHY: Calling the override through the new base contract raises TypeError for an unexpected keyword. HOW: Add `assignment_source`/`**kwargs` to the override signatures (Jira, JiraServer, VSTS already accept **kwargs).

issues.descricao: Claims to_dict() returns a raw datetime for queued that fails JSON serialization when passed as Celery task kwargs.
The assignment_source parameter was added to the abstract sync_status_outbound instead of sync_assignee_outbound, which is the method that actually receives it.
Claims concrete integrations overriding should_sync(self, attribute) will raise TypeError at the new two-argument call in sync_assignee_outbound.
Claims a malformed assignment_source_dict makes from_dict return None, so should_sync fails open and re-enables the sync cycle.
test_to_dict asserts queued is not None, which is always true because queued has a default, so the assertion verifies nothing.
Claims passing AssignmentSource.to_dict() with a raw datetime to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async fails Sentry's bad-pickle check in tests and would break under a JSON serializer.

sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter that is never threaded through the status task or checked in should_sync, so status sync gets no cycle prevention despite the signature suggesting it.
The base sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter but ExampleIntegration's override takes no **kwargs, so callers passing assignment_source would raise TypeError.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `get_committable_offsets` scans `range(start, max+1)` every second while `all_offsets` grows without bound when the head is stuck. WHY: One slow/poison offset makes each commit tick O(gap) CPU plus unbounded set memory, stalling all partition commits. HOW: Track contiguous completion incrementally instead of rescanning the full range, and cap or expire stuck heads.

WHAT: `wait_until_empty` returns True when `qsize()` is zero even though a dequeued item is still being processed. WHY: `OrderedQueueWorker.run` calls `get()` before `result_processor` and `complete_offset`, so any waiter observes an empty queue during the whole processing window and proceeds prematurely. HOW: also require no outstanding offsets (or track in-flight count / `unfinished_tasks`) before reporting empty.

issues.descricao: Claims queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown() are unavailable on Python < 3.13, so workers never exit on shutdown.
Claims Python's randomized str hash makes group-to-queue assignment differ across processes, breaking per-subscription ordering and letting two processes handle the same subscription concurrently.
Claims FixedQueuePool.submit leaks an outstanding offset when put() raises after add_offset, permanently blocking commits for the partition.
Claims get_stats/wait_until_empty report empty while items are still in flight because qsize drops when a worker takes an item.
Claims metrics.incr receives len(committable) as the instance argument instead of the amount, so the commit count is always 1.
The offsets_committed metric is incremented by the number of partitions being committed rather than the number of offsets, so its name misdescribes the value.
Claims factory shutdown leaves SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy commit threads running and committing after shutdown.
Claims the committable-offset loop iterates the whole numeric span max_offset - start, burning CPU on large offset gaps every commit cycle.
_get_partition_lock reads and writes partition_locks without a global lock, claimed to let two threads create different locks for one partition and break offset tracking.
States review of queue_consumer.py is incomplete with no issue found.
States review of result_consumer.py is incomplete with no issue found.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Plural *_ids branch calls obj[k].map without null/array guard. WHY: A null or missing ids payload throws TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole record.

issues.descricao: Claims expandable_first_post? lost its 'embeddable hosts configured' guard and now expands first posts when no EmbeddableHost exists.
Claims the plural *_ids hydration branch crashes on non-array values and keeps undefined entries for missing ids.
Claims Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing, so the client's saveChanges appears to succeed without saving.
Claims EmbeddingSerializer emits only embeddable_host_ids without sideloading the host records, so the admin host table renders empty.

_hydrateEmbedded now treats every `_ids` key as an embedded collection: it calls `.map` without a null/array check (TypeError on null) and always deletes the original key, replacing real id arrays with undefined lookups when the root has no matching collection.
RestAdapter.basePath replaces only the first underscore of the model type, so an admin model type with several underscores would not match ADMIN_MODELS and would use the wrong base path.
EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false on bad input and TopicEmbed.import calls eh.try(:category_id), which is claimed to raise on FalseClass and crash the import for malformed URLs.
Embed host checks now issue a database query via EmbeddableHost.record_for_host on every embed request instead of the previous in-memory site-setting check.
TopicEmbed.import passes a nil category when no embeddable host matches the URL, dropping the old embed_category default.
save_host replaces category_id 0 with the uncategorized category because it uses blank? instead of nil?.
The host input placeholder 'example.com' is hard-coded instead of using I18n.
The EmbeddableHostsController spec only checks inheritance and does not exercise create, update or destroy.
The EmbeddingController spec only checks inheritance and does not exercise show or update.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` raises NoMethodError when the setting is nil and `locale` passes through un-normalized so string/symbol duplicates are not deduped. WHY: The fallback chain is evaluated on every translate and `ensure_loaded!` runs on every request, so a nil or mistyped locale breaks all rendering. HOW: Normalize with presence-safe `to_sym` on both values before `compact.uniq`.

WHAT: The new `ensure_loaded!` forwards `I18n.locale`/`default_locale` into `load_locale` which interpolates it into `Regexp.new`. WHY: The new per-request preload in `set_locale` makes attacker-influenced locale hit the regex sink without escaping, enabling regex injection and over-broad translation file loading. HOW: Escape with `Regexp.escape(locale.to_s)` in `load_locale` and validate locale against supported locales before loading.

issues.descricao: Claims a fallback value cached for a not-yet-loaded locale stays stale after that locale's file is loaded, because ensure_loaded! does not invalidate the translation cache.
Suggests normalizing the locale because a String locale mixed with Symbol fallback entries defeats uniq and causes double lookups or double loading.
Claims a nil default_locale makes FallbackLocaleList#[] raise NoMethodError on every missing translation.
Claims every fallback lookup hits the database or Redis through SiteSetting.default_locale, amplifying per-request load.
Claims a user-controlled locale with regex metacharacters reaches load_locale's Regexp and forces loading of unintended locale files.
Claims @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and shared across threads without synchronization.
I18n.ensure_loaded! reads and initializes @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX, racing with reload!/load_locale under concurrent requests.
Claims set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (application_controller.rb:159) raises NoMethodError on every request if I18n.fallbacks is not the custom FallbackLocaleList.
FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but leaves it empty, so iterating I18n.fallbacks returns nothing.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Template iterates bare members while route sets model to the Group object. WHY: Without a controller alias the list renders empty and member rows never appear. HOW: Iterate model.members or add a controller alias.

WHAT: Bare members routes under resources provide :id while actions require :group_id. WHY: Real requests raise missing-param errors though specs calling actions directly pass. HOW: Use a member block or read params[:id].

issues.descricao: Claims the now-unawaited findMembers() call creates a race where the controller has no member data available when it needs it.
Claims the public group members template iterates a bare members property that resolves to undefined because the controller's model is now the Group object.
Claims add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] while the route supplies the group id as params[:id], so the actions always fail with ParameterMissing.
Claims add_members does not strip whitespace around comma-separated usernames, so entries like 'alice, bob' silently fail to add members.
Claims the public members endpoint accepts an unbounded or negative limit/offset, letting a caller force loading and serializing the whole membership of a large group.
params[:alias_level].present? is false for 0, so choosing the 'nobody' alias level is ignored.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: OAuth authorize includes redirect_uri but the code-for-token exchange omits it. WHY: GitHub cannot bind the code to the expected redirect, weakening code-redemption validation against code interception or redirect mismatch. HOW: Include the same absolute redirect_uri in the token-exchange data.

issues.descricao: Claims the OAuth state is compared to the secret pipeline signature in non-constant time, leaking timing information.
Claims other consumers driving GitHubInstallation without the new OAuth view will always be rejected; no such consumer exists.
Claims a null reference when the github_authenticated_user state is missing; the code only compares it and returns the error page.
test_github_user_mismatch asserts only the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message, which any error path would produce.
The GitHub OAuth state parameter is compared with != instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information.
The installation sender-login mismatch test asserts only the generic error text, which state mismatch and OAuth failures also produce, so it cannot show the login check caused the rejection.
The OAuth state check in GitHub OAuthLoginView compares the callback state to pipeline.signature with a plain `!=` instead of a constant-time comparison.
Claims the GitHub OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri, so GitHub returns redirect_uri_mismatch and every installation fails.
Claims a literal 'null' installation_id passes the None check and routes users to the 'Invalid installation request.' page instead of the app installer.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `grantType` is snapshotted in the constructor but `setFormParams` never refreshes it. WHY: Any caller replacing form params leaves a stale grant that is then persisted via `createTokenResponse` into the encoded token ID. HOW: Re-derive `grantType` inside `setFormParams`.

issues.descricao: Claims setFormParams replaces form params without refreshing the cached grantType, leaving getGrantType() stale.
getShortcut() is added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation, breaking existing custom grant type factories when the encoder factory calls it.
Token context encoding calls getShouldUseLightweightToken on every token creation, which dereferences the session context client and would NPE where no client is set.
initToken always encodes the token id and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for a grant type without a registered shortcut, so custom or unmapped grants would fail token issuance with a 500.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Federated-first lookup combined with write-fallback creates split-brain credentials with no cleanup of the losing copy. WHY: Regenerating codes for a federated user that does not support the type creates a local credential that `getCredential` then ignores in favor of the old federated one, so new codes never validate and old codes stay live.

WHAT: The federated write path hands JSON of raw recovery codes as `challengeResponse` for external storage. WHY: External providers persist that value verbatim as retrievable secrets while the local path hashes codes, exposing plaintext recoverable credentials in third-party storage.

issues.descricao: Claims the recovery-code validator uses non-constant-time String.equals, leaking timing information about stored codes.
Claims raw recovery codes are serialized and persisted in cleartext in user storage instead of hashed.
Claims Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without isPresent() can throw NoSuchElementException.
Plaintext recovery codes are serialized and sent to user storage providers via updateCredential, while the local path stores only hashed codes.
Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext instead of hashed, so a provider may persist working second-factor codes.
The test user storage accepts any of the user's recovery codes rather than the specific requested code number, unlike the local provider.
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, so it throws NullPointerException for a user missing from the provider's map.
Claims recovery code verification compares hashes with String.equals, enabling timing attacks.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based while order is 0-based but the mixin copies $val verbatim. WHY: Legacy WebKit/Firefox render .panel order(3) and .extra-info-wrapper order(2) shifted by one, misordering header items. HOW: Emit $val + 1 for the ordinal-group properties while keeping order/$val for the modern properties.

issues.descricao: Claims the order mixin's box-ordinal-group values are off by one versus order, so legacy WebKit/Firefox render a different item order.
Making .small-action a flex container is claimed to make the floated buttons ignore float:right, because they would be flex items, so they collapse next to the description.
Claims that removing the 5px bullet margin in .extra-info-wrapper misaligns category bullets because the wrapper's parent is still float-based and order() has no effect.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Direct dict access raises KeyError when the field is absent. WHY: One malformed span poisons the whole batch and blocks offset commit/retries. HOW: Fall back to the message timestamp or a default via val.get.

issues.descricao: Claims the redirect-resolution limit was silently cut from 10000 to 1000, so segment trees deeper than 1000 are no longer joined, and the comment still mentions 10k.
Claims a non-root span whose key equals the resolved set key unions the key with itself and then unlinks it, deleting the buffered segment.
Claims a span message missing end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError and aborts the whole batch.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch passes cursor.offset directly into queryset slicing when advanced features are enabled.
Claims BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset to an unclamped offset for previous-page cursors, allowing negative slicing.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies floor/ceil to a datetime key, raising TypeError.
Claims accessing organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError when organization_context is None.
process_batch indexes end_timestamp_precise directly, so a span without the field raises KeyError and fails the whole consumer batch.
Claims span_count counts pre-existing spans in set_key, so zpopmin evicts far more than the overflow above 1000 and discards valid spans.
SDK-supplied end_timestamp_precise is used as the ZSET eviction score, so an attacker sending far-future timestamps could keep their spans and force eviction of legitimate ones.
Each span insert runs up to two ZUNIONSTORE copies of the segment set plus ZCARD/ZPOPMIN, making segment building O(N^2) on the ingest hot path.
Claims end_timestamp_precise is not validated as finite before being used as a ZADD score.
Claims test_backpressure uses identical end_timestamp_precise values and so cannot catch timestamp-ordering or eviction regressions.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics dereference req without nil check. WHY: A nil request panics at req.PluginContext while sibling LoggerMiddleware explicitly handles nil, showing nil reaches this layer. HOW: Add the same nil guard delegating to next.

issues.descricao: Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil requests because it reads req.PluginContext without a nil guard.
Claims the refactor dropped traceID from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines.
Claims the metrics middleware factory mutates a shared instance's next field, causing a data race between chains.
Claims the request-size histogram's HELP text says 'returned' though it measures request sizes.
Claims the test never asserts that request size is not instrumented for CheckHealth/CollectMetrics.
Claims checkHistogram carries foundLabels across metrics and returns errors prematurely.
Claims millisecond durations are truncated by integer division before conversion to float.
Claims the request-size test cases use empty payloads and would not detect a broken size calculation.
Claims the duration metric checks only labels and sample counts, not the observed values.
Claims the duration-seconds histogram check omits status and source labels.
Claims LoggerMiddleware depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running first and would log without plugin identity if reordered.
Claims the metrics middleware now fails the request when the plugin is not in the registry.
The metrics middleware test never asserts that request size is not recorded for CheckHealth and CollectMetrics.
MetricsMiddleware dereferences req (req.Queries, req.Body, req.PluginContext) without a nil-request guard, unlike LoggerMiddleware, so a nil request would panic.
QueryData and CallResource look up the plugin in the registry twice per request.
Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware is wasted work when backend request logging is disabled because only LoggerMiddleware consumes its context attributes.

sugestoes.texto: Aggregate flush capacity grows linearly with process count because each subprocess divides the global limit by its subset size instead of the global shard count. Scale the per-process budget by the global shard count so total flushed segments stay bounded.

issues.descricao: Splitting the buffer per process makes spans.buffer.max-flush-segments a per-process cap, so with P flusher processes up to P times the configured segments are loaded and flushed per cycle.
Claims the CLI default of 1 makes the one-process-per-shard auto mode unreachable.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Same-domain branch builds display as host plus URI path only, discarding query string and fragment. WHY: A same-domain website like example.com/user?ref=1 displays as example.com/user, losing distinguishing URL information. HOW: Append query and fragment from the parsed URI when building website_name.

issues.descricao: The www.example.com vs forum.example.com branch of website_name is not tested.
The scheme-less website case (nil host) of website_name is not tested.
Claims the suffix check `"." << website_host` mutates website_host by prepending a dot, so unrelated domains are displayed as ".example.com" and the new unrelated-domain spec fails.
website_name parses the website with URI and returns nil when there is no scheme, so a website like example.com/user disappears from the profile.
The same-domain website label concatenates only host and path, dropping the query string and fragment so the label differs from the link.
Claims website_name silently swallows URI parse errors without logging.
